exercises.title: No capital letters
exercises.body: Shavian has no capitals at all — a sentence simply starts with its first letter. Everything else you already know carries over: full stops, commas and question marks are borrowed from English unchanged. Now that the answers are whole sentences, the keyboard offers whichever of those marks a sentence needs, beside the naming dot.

exercises.title: The dot still marks a name
exercises.body: With no capitals to lean on, the naming dot does that work: it goes in front of every name, wherever it sits in the sentence. ·𐑕𐑨𐑥 at the start, ·𐑕𐑨𐑥 in the middle — always the dot.

exercises.title: The endings, now in your hand
exercises.body: Chapter 3 taught you to read the past tense; here you have to produce it. Nothing new to learn — just say the word before you write it, and let the ending follow. Walked ends voiceless, so 𐑢𐑷𐑒𐑑. Played hums, so 𐑐𐑤𐑱𐑛. Wanted has a beat of its own, so 𐑢𐑪𐑯𐑑𐑩𐑛.

exercises.title: You can write Shavian
exercises.body: That is the alphabet in both directions: you can read it and now you can write it. Everything from here is practice — and the fastest practice is the smallest, so write your shopping list in Shavian, or a note to yourself. Chapter 5 will take you further, into longer stories, accents and writing freely.
